summary: Pick E2B for microVMs in your own cloud, Daytona for Windows, macOS and GPU sandboxes, Modal for GPUs and million-sandbox bursts, and Tangle for installed coding agents that need no model key.

agents.label: Coding agents
agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, OpenClaw, Kimi Code and Prime Agent installed in every sandbox

prompt.label: Giving the agent a task
prompt.text: One prompt call returns the agent's result, token usage and cost

models.label: Model calls
models.text: Tangle Router by default, billed to the same Tangle balance as the sandbox

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.text: A container or a Firecracker microVM, chosen per sandbox

pause.label: Stop and resume
pause.text: Timers you set stop a sandbox; a stopped sandbox keeps its files until you delete it or its delete timer passes

snapshots.label: Snapshots and forks
snapshots.text: Snapshot, revert, and split a running sandbox into copies

desktop.label: Desktop
desktop.text: A desktop the coding agent controls through a hosted computer-use endpoint

gpu.label: GPUs
gpu.text: A GPU lease from a GPU cloud provider, attached while a command needs it, with a spend cap and a time cap

mcp.label: MCP
mcp.text: A local stdio MCP server for one sandbox, plus the hosted computer-use endpoint

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.text: Stored once; you choose whether the sandbox can read a secret or only the network proxy can

network.label: Network
network.text: Open, a strict allowlist, or blocked, changeable while the sandbox runs

terminals.label: Getting a shell
terminals.text: SSH, a PTY or a browser terminal

traces.label: Run records
traces.text: Every agent turn is traced, and an Intelligence report summarizes what the agent did

byoc.label: Your own cloud
byoc.text: Tangle hosts the sandboxes; on-premises hosting is planned. agent-runtime runs the same agent code on E2B, Daytona or any ComputeSDK cloud

sdks.label: SDKs
sdks.text: TypeScript, Python (tangle-sandbox on PyPI) and the tangle CLI

free.label: Free start
free.text: A Free plan with no included credit

soc2.label: Compliance
soc2.text: A SOC 2 Type II examination covering June 14 to September 14, 2026; the report is in issuance

rivals.name: E2B
rivals.summary: Pick E2B for a Firecracker microVM per session, sandboxes in your own AWS, GCP or Azure account, and memory kept across pause; pick Tangle when the coding agent should need no model key, return its result, usage and cost from one prompt call, and stop at a fleet budget you set in dollars.

pick.text: Every session needs its own microVM: E2B runs each sandbox on a Firecracker-based microVM with its own kernel.
Sandboxes must run in your AWS, GCP or Azure account, through E2B's enterprise BYOC, or on your own node with the Apache-2.0 E2B Embed package.
A paused sandbox must keep its memory, so running processes survive the resume.
You run in Asia-Pacific: E2B Cloud lists US, EU and APAC regions.
You want to start on free usage credit with no card, and run more sandboxes at once than Tangle's Free plan allows.
You want a platform many teams already run: E2B reports 2B+ sandboxes started and 100K+ teams.

pickTangle.text: Your coding agent needs no model key: Tangle Router is the default, billed to your Tangle balance.
One prompt call gives the agent its task and returns the result, token usage and cost.
A fleet runs many agents under one budget, set in dollars, and the platform refuses any charge past it.
You keep E2B as well: agent-runtime runs the same agent code on E2B and on Tangle.

rows.text: Pre-built templates for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Prime Agent, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Amp, Cursor Agents, Devin and more
You bring the model; the sandbox calls it under your egress policy
A Firecracker-based microVM with its own kernel for every sandbox
Pause keeps the filesystem and memory, so running processes survive, and a paused sandbox is kept with no automatic deletion
Snapshots capture filesystem and memory and start new sandboxes from that state
E2B Desktop: a screen, mouse and keyboard with a live stream
200+ MCP servers, called from inside the sandbox
A secrets vault: keys the agent can use but never read
Ingress and egress under your policy
Metrics, logs and signed webhooks
US, EU and APAC
BYOC in your AWS, GCP or Azure account for enterprise customers; E2B Embed runs the whole stack on one node
Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, plus Code Interpreter and Desktop SDKs
A Hobby tier with one-time usage credit and no card required
Lists SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA

published.text: E2B publishes usage, not a start time, on the pages linked here: 2B+ sandboxes started and 100K+ teams.

move.text: The migration guide maps each E2B call to Tangle, and E2B-compatible REST routes accept E2B's request and response shapes, so HTTP code can stay as it is.

rivals.name: Daytona
rivals.summary: Pick Daytona for Windows and macOS desktops, GPU sandboxes, five SDK languages and compute in your own cloud; pick Tangle for eight installed coding agents, one prompt call per task, and sandboxes, models and traces on one key.

pick.text: Your agent needs a Windows or macOS desktop as well as Linux.
You need a GPU inside the sandbox: Daytona has NVIDIA and AMD GPU sandboxes.
Your code is in Ruby, Go or Java: Daytona has SDKs for those as well as Python and TypeScript.
Sandboxes must run on compute in your own cloud, with Daytona running the control plane.
A paused VM sandbox must keep its memory, or you fork a running state.
Start time decides it: Daytona states sub-90 ms sandbox creation, and our measured times below are slower.
You want free compute credit to start.

pickTangle.text: You want Pi, Hermes, Kimi Code or Prime Agent next to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw, installed in every sandbox.
One prompt call gives the agent its task and returns the result, token usage and cost.
Sandboxes, model calls and traces go on one key and one balance.
A fleet runs many agents under one budget, set in dollars, and the platform refuses any charge past it.
You keep Daytona as well: agent-runtime runs the same agent code on Daytona and on Tangle.

rows.text: Default snapshots include the Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw packages
Not found on the Daytona pages we read
Container sandboxes; Linux VM, Windows, GPU and macOS sandboxes
Persistent by default; VM sandboxes pause and resume with memory, and container sandboxes keep their files across stop and start; GPU sandboxes are deleted on stop
Cold snapshots of the filesystem; hot snapshots and forks with memory on VM sandboxes
Linux, Windows and macOS desktops you control with code
NVIDIA and AMD GPU sandboxes
An MCP server set up for Claude, Cursor and Windsurf
Plaintext credentials stay outside the sandbox and are substituted at network egress
Domain and IP allowlists or block all, set per sandbox on Tiers 3 and 4 (Tiers 1 and 2 use the organization's restrictions), and an outbound proxy set at create time
SSH, a web terminal, VS Code in the browser and language-server support
Traces, logs and metrics from inside sandboxes, exported over OpenTelemetry
Shared US and EU regions, plus dedicated and custom regions
Customer-managed compute in your cloud, with Daytona's control plane
Python, TypeScript, Ruby, Go and Java
Free compute credit included
States it meets HIPAA, SOC 2 and GDPR standards

published.text: Daytona states "Sub 90ms sandbox creation from code to execution" on its home page.

move.text: The migration guide maps each Daytona call and setting to Tangle and shows a typical Daytona program on Tangle.

rivals.name: Modal
rivals.summary: Pick Modal for GPU sandboxes, million-sandbox bursts, and inference and training on the same platform; pick Tangle for eight coding agents, installed in every sandbox and needing no model key, and sandboxes that stop and resume with their files.

pick.text: You need very large bursts: Modal states it creates over a million sandboxes in under a minute and runs up to 1M at once.
The sandbox needs a GPU: Modal runs GPU sandboxes on its gVisor runtime.
You also serve or train models: Modal offers inference, training and sandboxes on one platform.
You need Docker inside the sandbox: Modal's VM runtime runs it.
You want capacity in many regions: Modal spans 20+ clouds and routes work to a region.
You want free credit every month: the Starter plan includes monthly credits.

pickTangle.text: You want the coding agent already there: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, OpenClaw, Kimi Code and Prime Agent are installed in every sandbox.
One prompt call gives the agent its task and returns the result, token usage and cost.
A sandbox should stop and resume with its files, which it keeps until you delete it or its delete timer passes.
Your coding agent needs no model key: Tangle Router is the default, billed to your Tangle balance.

rows.text: Not stated in Modal's Sandboxes guide, which builds sandboxes from images you define
Modal Inference serves open models on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or your own inference stack
gVisor, or a VM runtime for Docker, FUSE and kernel features; Modal chooses when you leave it unset
A sandbox ends at a timeout you set, up to a cap in Modal's guide
Filesystem and Directory Snapshots; Memory Snapshots in alpha, kept 7 days
GPU sandboxes on the gVisor runtime
Secret injection, in beta: headers are added to outbound requests outside the sandbox, so the secret never appears in it
Logs and metrics for every sandbox, exportable to OpenTelemetry
Capacity across 20+ clouds; Modal routes work to a region
Python, plus JavaScript and Go SDKs in beta
Monthly free credits on the Starter plan
Lists SOC 2 Type II and states it is HIPAA ready

published.text: Modal states "Create over a million Sandboxes in under a minute, and run up to 1M concurrently" and "Sub-second starts on large custom images and at high concurrency".
Modal's engineering post of 2026-07-16 reports sandbox start times under half a second at the median in its 1M-sandbox test, and says the tail is longer than it would like.
